attempted_claim: For every odd prime p let G_p = C_{p^2} \oplus C_{p^2} of exponent p^2. Let s_{+-}(G_p) be the smallest l such that every sequence over G_p of length l has a {+1,-1}-weighted zero-sum subsequence of length exactly p^2. Determine the exact integer s_{+-}(G_p) as a function of p and classify all extremal sequences of length s_{+-}(G_p)-1 with no such weighted zero-sum, via an explicit Chevalley--Warning / combinatorial Nullstellenssatz polynomial system. A complete answer proves the exact value for all odd p and the full extremal form up to automorphism and signs.
decisive_failure: The natural selector-based Chevalley-Warning system controls length only modulo p and sums only modulo p, and every bounded-degree repair overflowed the degree budget; computation covered only p=3 with a single verified avoider plus bounded random sampling, far short of an all-p exact value and classification.
